title: Two games in the same Next Fest, both built in Godot with Claude Code in under a year, by one person with a day job. What the AI did, what it didn't, and which game it helped more
author: EndpaperDev
selftext:
I'm one person in Somerset with a day job and two demos in Next Fest until Monday. The Infinite Library is an incremental about a library that reads itself. Faultfinder is a deduction game about debugging a dead engineer's program. Same framework, same ten months, very different weeks.

![img](dj54e5zlq8xh1 "Faultfinder - Event Header")

![gif](nbm3tjw1r8xh1 "The Infinite Library - Event GIF")

I wrote the design docs myself first, in chat, before any code. I think that's the bit people skip and then wonder why the agent builds the wrong game.

Claude Code wrote nearly all the GDScript for both. I review, I rarely write. What made it work was building a small framework first (skills, hooks, rules, templates) and writing every lesson back into it. Ten months on, the framework is the asset.

The bit I'm proudest of is a playtest bot that drives the real UI and presses the actual buttons. It started as build checking. It ended up recording my Next Fest broadcast with --write-movie, with captions placed off its frame log. Gotcha: --write-movie doesn't reach the game as an argument, so my first renders were silent!

Faultfinder taught me where AI testing stops. I had model-driven personas play the demo in a browser. Clean timings, 7 to 18 minutes a case. Then real telemetry came in and three quarters of players' wrong answers were on one clause the personas almost never got wrong. A model reads a trace too well to stand in for a person. I kept them for regression and stopped using them for difficulty.

![gif](m7rhqbvnq8xh1 "Faultfinder - the debugging loop")

What AI didn't do: every word in both games is mine. The Library's key art is a commissioned illustration, after I replaced an AI capsule that looked fine until I saw it next to a drawn one. Some in-game art and the music are generated, disclosed on both pages. Marketing copy is where I'm least comfortable. Claude drafts, I rewrite, people still say it reads as AI.

Numbers. Both demos get about 1% from the fest grid, so Steam treats them the same. Then they split. Faultfinder went 405 to 779 wishlists in four days and is #63 most played puzzle demo. The Library went 455 to 523 in the same four days. But 36% who start the Library finish it, and most Faultfinder players never clear case one. One gets found and not held, one gets held and not found. Same tools, same person, so I've stopped blaming the pipeline either way.

Both free demos: 

The Infinite Library: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4693700/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4693700/) 

Faultfinder: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5120320/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5120320/)

Happy to answer anything about the bot or the personas. I don't see many people doing the bot and I think they should!
